reader.requirement: At 1985, an indexed (and relative) file control entry with no ACCESS MODE clause must have sequential access: format 1 READ only (no KEY / INVALID KEY), WRITEs in ascending prime-key order, REWRITE/DELETE of the last record read, START allowed.

edition-consulted.site: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/KeyedIoEmitter.cs#EmitRegistration (ctx.Data.DialectLevel passed to FileRegistry.RegisterIndexed as the connector's Edition)
edition-consulted.switches: carries the edition into the connector for the DialectBehavior tests; access mode itself is passed edition-blind

reader.edition-search: The default is the FileModel.AccessMode initializer (Sequential), set only by MapAccessMode when the clause is written; grepped AccessMode/AccessModeWritten across Compiler, ConstructRegistry.g.cs (no access-mode construct), ReservedWords (DYNAMIC continuous since 1985), DialectBehavior (no access-mode behaviour): the default path consults no edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness pins sequential READ order and the ascending-WRITE requirement; the refusal of format 2 READ/INVALID KEY, REWRITE/DELETE without prior READ, relative files and a READ after a failed OPEN are not exercised

probes.printed: COBOL0864 READ KEY on 'IX': the file's access mode is SEQUENTIAL (the ACCESS MODE clause is not specified, so sequential access is assumed ...)
probes.expected: refused: §1985:IX.4.5.3 SR4 format 1 only under sequential access

probes.printed: COBOL1720 on READ ... INVALID KEY and on DELETE ... INVALID KEY
probes.expected: refused: both are format-2 / random-only phrases under sequential access

probes.printed: W3-INVALID W3=21 (equal key); DEL-NO-READ=43; REW-KEYCHG=21; REW-OK=43 (last statement was a failed REWRITE); START=00 R2=00 BB02; relative RL1=00 R01 RL2=00 R02 RL3=10; NF-OPEN=35 NF-READ=47
probes.expected: sequential-access semantics for indexed and relative files; READ after failed OPEN 47

probes.printed: VX=00 08 [K1ABCDEF] / VX=00 04 [K2XY    ] (RECORD VARYING indexed, no ACCESS clause)
probes.expected: records read sequentially with their lengths

probes.printed: COBOL0900 a RELATIVE KEY clause that is not a phrase of the ACCESS MODE clause requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: at 1985 RELATIVE KEY exists only as a phrase of ACCESS MODE

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.2.4.4 GR1  the text is in GR1
OK  §1985:IX.4.5.3 SR4  the text is in SR4

reader.notes: The default is structural (FileModel.AccessMode = Sequential) and every verb's branch reads it, so an omitted clause behaves exactly as ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL. The COBOL0864 message cites §2023 text, but the behaviour is the 1985 rule's.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-091/src/rd_seq.cob (run rd_seq-001), indexed file with no ACCESS MODE clause: SORT ... USING SQ GIVING IX gave 00; OPEN EXTEND 00, then WRITE of AB (below the highest key) took INVALID KEY 21 and WRITE DD gave 00 (OK §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR14 'released to the mass storage control system (MSCS) in ascending order of prime record key values'); REWRITE ... INVALID KEY compiled and a key change answered 21; START NOT LESS THAN then READ gave 00 BB02; DELETE after a REWRITE (not a READ) gave 43 (§1985:IX.4.3.4 GR2, which cite.py names after it refused GR3); SORT USING IX GIVING SQ DESCENDING gave DD04, CC03, BBXX, AA01. Probe ra_native.cob: the 7th WRITE, out of order, gave 21. Grepped FileControlBinder.cs for Edition/CobolVersion/DialectBehavior/Constructs: no access-mode edition switch, so the reader's edition-blind default holds. OK §1985:IX.2.4.4 GR1 'sequential access is assumed'.
